content.text:
Good places to find **latest stock market news**:

- **Reuters Markets** — best for fast, relatively neutral market-moving headlines and global context. ([investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/shares-hesitant-after-us-jobs-data-oil-jumps-on-venezuela-blockade-4411720?utm_source=openai))  
- **CNBC Markets** — good for live market updates, TV clips, analyst commentary, and U.S. market coverage. ([cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/?msockid=0de07ec2e0ed6f4238d66885e16d6eb7&utm_source=openai))  
- **MarketWatch** — accessible summaries of U.S. stocks, bonds, personal finance, and company-specific market news. ([morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch?utm_source=openai))  
- **The Wall Street Journal / Bloomberg / Financial Times** — excellent professional coverage, though much is paywalled.  
- **Yahoo Finance or Google Finance** — useful if you want headlines next to charts, watchlists, and stock quotes.  
- **StockAnalysis.com News** — a free aggregator that pulls together market and company news from multiple outlets. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/news/?utm_source=openai))  

If you want **real-time price moves**, use your brokerage app, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC, or Bloomberg. If you want **serious market analysis**, Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, and FT are usually stronger than social media or Reddit.
